clue.text: River Island stock emptied in plant

parts.note: the Tamar is the river dividing Devon from Cornwall

indicators.note: emptied means the word stock loses all its inner letters, leaving its shell

parts.note: only the first and last letters are kept

explanation.surface: A high-street fashion chain's stock, cleared out, sitting among the plants; Stir It Up and other Catch a Fire tracks echo through the puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: River Island is a British clothing chain, but here the two words split into separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The tamarisk is a feathery shrub of salty coasts and deserts, an example of a plant.

clue.text: Stop that train, primarily about hard struggle

indicators.note: about means the first letters go round the next pieces
primarily picks the first letter of each of that and train

parts.note: the first letters of these two words
war is a struggle or conflict

explanation.surface: An attempt to halt a train, like the Wailers' Stop That Train, after a hard struggle.
explanation.definitionFit: To thwart something is to frustrate it, to stop it succeeding.

clue.text: No more trouble for rear shower

definitions.note: a person who shows the rear, read cryptically

indicators.note: trouble means disturb, so the letters of no more are mixed up

parts.note: the letters of these two words are the fodder

explanation.surface: No more trouble, a Wailers title, caused by someone baring their backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shower' reads as a bath fitting, but is one who shows.
explanation.definitionFit: A mooner bares their buttocks as a prank, so is literally someone showing their bottom.

clue.text: Bob Marley perhaps managed star touring America

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the rearranged letters circle America's letter
managed means handled, so the letters of star are rearranged

parts.note: the word itself is the fodder

explanation.surface: Bob Marley as a managed star touring the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Bob Marley was a devout Rastafarian, so an example of a Rasta.

clue.text: Endurance of Anita Harris finally cracked over mile

indicators.note: over means the rearranged letters lie over the mile, enclosing it
cracked means broken, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the name itself is part of the fodder

indicators.note: finally gives the last letter of Harris

parts.note: its last letter joins the fodder

explanation.surface: Anita Harris's endurance finally gives out over a mile run.
explanation.walkthrough: Anita Harris is a British singer and actress.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamina is staying power, the capacity for sustained effort.

clue.text: Kiki maybe grasping answer in 400 years

indicators.note: grasping means the singer's surname holds the next part between its letters

parts.note: Kiki Dee is a British pop singer, so 'Kiki maybe' is a Dee

indicators.note: the answer letter sits in the middle of the Roman numerals for 400

parts.note: CD is 400 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A singer clutching the answer to the Wailers' song 400 Years.
explanation.walkthrough: '400 years' reads as one phrase, a Catch a Fire track title, but 400 is wordplay and 'years' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A decade is a period of ten years, so it can stand for years.

clue.text: Earwig left out of shed in autumn?

definitions.note: used as a verb: to listen in secretly

indicators.note: out of means the letter for left is taken away

parts.note: read cryptically: what happens in autumn is that leaves drop

explanation.surface: An earwig crawling out of a garden shed in autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: Earwig looks like the insect; it is an informal verb for listening in. 'Shed' is a verb, not the hut.
explanation.definitionFit: To earwig is British slang for overhearing other people's private conversation.

clue.text: Secured a new job with degree

parts.note: taken as written
a chore is a routine task or job

explanation.surface: Someone landing a new job thanks to a degree.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship anchored is held fast, so anchored means fixed or secured.

clue.text: Head of Exeter City in America welcoming minister to appeal

indicators.note: head of gives the first letter of Exeter

parts.note: its first letter only

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so the city holds the next word

parts.note: NY, New York
to minister to someone is to treat them

explanation.surface: The chairman of Exeter City football club in America invites a government minister to make an appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: Exeter City is a football club, but the words split into separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An entreaty is an earnest request or plea, an appeal.

clue.text: Club's getting 50% from Norman Hunter

parts.note: a wood is a golf club; with the 's it gives WOODS

indicators.note: 50% from means half of the name Norman is dropped, leaving its second half

parts.note: the name itself, of which only the latter half survives

explanation.surface: A football club's star gets half the credit from the Leeds hard man Norman Hunter.
explanation.walkthrough: Norman Hunter was a famously tough Leeds United defender, so the name looks like a single footballer; 'Hunter' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodsman lives and works in the forest, traditionally a trapper or hunter.

clue.text: High octave for bird

indicators.note: high here means intoxicated, so the letters of octave are scrambled

parts.note: the word itself is the fodder

explanation.surface: A high octave sung by a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocet is a black-and-white wading bird with an upturned bill.

clue.text: Jump about in concrete jungle

indicators.note: about means the letters found there are read backwards
in shows the letters sit within concrete jungle

parts.note: the letters run across the end of concrete into jungle

explanation.surface: Leaping around a concrete jungle, as in the Wailers' song.
explanation.definitionFit: A jeté is a ballet leap from one foot to the other, a kind of jump.

clue.text: Maxine Peake's back performing after concerning review

indicators.note: after means the anagram follows the word for concerning

parts.note: RE, as in a memo heading, means concerning

indicators.note: performing suggests acting out, so the letters are put to work in a new order

parts.note: the name itself is part of the fodder

indicators.note: back gives the last letter of Peake, the 's being a link

parts.note: its last letter joins the fodder

explanation.surface: The actress Maxine Peake returns to the stage after a review of her work.
explanation.walkthrough: Maxine Peake is a British actor, which makes 'performing' look literal.
explanation.definitionFit: To review something is to look it over again, to examine it a second time.

clue.text: See 27
Some held captive by slave-driver rejected God

indicators.note: rejected means the hidden run is turned round
only some of the letters, held inside slave-driver, are used

parts.note: the letters straddle the two halves of the hyphenated word

explanation.surface: A slave-driver, like the Wailers' song, rejects God while holding people captive.
explanation.definitionFit: A deva is a deity or benevolent spirit in Hindu and Buddhist belief.

clue.text: Particular society falling down completely for the chosen ones

indicators.note: falling down completely means the society letter drops from the top to the very bottom

parts.note: particular means choosy, selective
the society letter, put back at the very end

explanation.surface: A selective club collapsing entirely for its chosen members.
explanation.walkthrough: In this down clue, S for society moves from the start of the word to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Electives are optional subjects or courses that students pick for themselves.

clue.text: Sincere pledge

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a token or deposit given as a guarantee of more to come

explanation.definitionFit: Earnest money is a down payment that binds a bargain; as an adjective the word means serious in intent.

clue.text: Vegetable seeds occasionally grew

parts.note: a sprout, a Brussels sprout, is a vegetable

indicators.note: occasionally means taking every other letter of seeds

parts.note: its second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: Vegetable seeds sprouting now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprouted means put out shoots, so began to grow.

clue.text: Bums around India in briefs

indicators.note: around means the dossers surround the letter for India

parts.note: dossers are tramps, bums
India is I in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Bottoms wrapped in underpants in India.
explanation.walkthrough: Bums and briefs suggest underwear; a dosser is British slang for a vagrant.
explanation.definitionFit: A dossier is a file of documents, as a lawyer's brief is.

clue.text: Demo upset Peter Tosh — he's leaving!

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the remaining letters are rearranged
leaving means these two letters walk out of the name

parts.note: the name itself is the fodder
the two letters of he are struck out of the name

explanation.surface: Wailer Peter Tosh storms out of the band in a huff.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is': he is leaving Peter Tosh, the Wailers guitarist who left the group.
explanation.definitionFit: A demo, short for demonstration, is a public protest march.

clue.text: Jack without energy to run fast

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the sailor goes round energy

parts.note: a jack tar is a sailor, as is a tar

explanation.surface: Jack, out of energy, trying to run quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: To tear along is to rush at great speed.

clue.text: Brazilians stir it up

indicators.note: stir means mix, so the letters of it up are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these two words are the fodder

explanation.surface: Brazilians urged to stir it up, the Wailers' song.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tupi are an Indigenous people of Brazil, so the name covers a group of Brazilians.

clue.text: Switched tee on tricky dogleg

parts.note: the letter T is spelt tee

indicators.note: tricky means awkward, so the letters of dogleg are rearranged

parts.note: the word itself is the fodder

explanation.surface: A golfer changing tee on an awkward dogleg hole.
explanation.walkthrough: A dogleg is a golf hole that bends, and the tee looks like the golf peg.
explanation.definitionFit: To toggle is to switch between two states, as with a button.

clue.text: Bunny wailer's ultimate 'rock it baby' cut short

indicators.note: ultimate gives the last letter of wailer, the 's being a possessive link

parts.note: its last letter only

indicators.note: rock means shake, so the letters are rearranged
cut short means the last letter of baby is dropped

parts.note: the words themselves, less the final letter, are the fodder

explanation.surface: Bunny Wailer's final take on Rock It Baby gets cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: Bunny Wailer was a founder of the Wailers, and Rock It Baby a Catch a Fire song; here 'Bunny' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Bunny is a child's word for a rabbit.

clue.text: Fiddler missing introduction to catch a fire?

indicators.note: missing means that letter is taken away

parts.note: one who fiddles is a cheater

indicators.note: introduction to gives the first letter of catch

parts.note: its first letter only

explanation.surface: A violinist trying to catch fire, nodding to the album Catch a Fire.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain an electric fire is a room heater.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas or electric fire is a domestic heating appliance.

clue.text: Inception on TV

parts.note: taken as written
a TV set is a set

explanation.walkthrough: Inception, the film, looks to be on television; it is the beginning of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Onset is a synonym for the start or beginning of something.

clue.text: Total giant oddly into kinky reggae

indicators.note: into means those odd letters go inside the reworked reggae
kinky means twisted, so the letters of reggae are rearranged

parts.note: the word itself is the fodder

indicators.note: oddly gives the first, third and fifth letters of giant

parts.note: its odd-numbered letters

explanation.surface: A giant total for the Wailers' track Kinky Reggae.
explanation.definitionFit: An aggregate is a sum or overall total, as in a two-legged football tie.

clue.text: Nationalist abandons cultural belief

indicators.note: abandons means that letter leaves the word

parts.note: ethnic means relating to a cultural group

explanation.surface: A nationalist giving up a cultural belief.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethic is a moral principle or set of values, a belief about right conduct.

clue.text: 240 midnight ravers at last getting substance

parts.note: midnight is twelve o'clock

indicators.note: at last gives only the final letter of ravers

parts.note: its last letter only
the core of something is its substance or essence

explanation.surface: Two hundred and forty midnight ravers, as in the Wailers' song, finally getting stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: Midnight Ravers is the closing track of Catch a Fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is twenty, so twelve of them make two hundred and forty.

clue.text: Characters in mountain hospital getting aid wrongly

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain
to abet is to help someone commit wrongdoing

explanation.surface: Characters in a mountain hospital who give bad help.
explanation.definitionFit: An alphabet is the set of letters, or characters, used to write a language.

clue.text: Inspectors exercise neglect

parts.note: DI is a detective inspector, so DIS are inspectors
to exercise a right is to use it

explanation.surface: Police inspectors using their powers through neglect.
explanation.definitionFit: Disuse is the state of no longer being used, the result of neglect.

clue.text: Wacky redcoat entertaining posh teacher

indicators.note: entertaining means holding a guest, so the posh letter sits inside
wacky means crazy, so the letters of redcoat are scrambled

parts.note: the word itself is the fodder
U stands for upper class, so posh

explanation.surface: A zany holiday-camp entertainer amusing a posh teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: A redcoat is an entertainer at a Butlin's holiday camp, which fits 'entertaining' in the surface.
